wasabi -- drive an Amiga from a Linux / macOS / BSD machine over the network
(Tobias Karlsson, MIT licence: LICENSE). Source: https://github.com/creep-ltx/wasabi;
UP-Term builds from its fork https://github.com/spotUP/wasabi.

  wasabid        the daemon, for the Amiga: wasabid 0.11b2 (17.10.2026) plus the
                 fork's unreleased MUI group-button listing, commit
                 562672a8a24b2d874301da15277e15bd824dd5c6, built by UP-Term from that
                 source (make wasabi, Bebbo's m68k-amigaos-gcc, the 68000 build; the
                 pin is tools/nas/wasabi.rev). Install puts it in C: when asked,
                 with a key of its own, started at every boot. It replaces the
                 wasabid 0.2 and the amiagent of earlier kits.
  wasabi         the client, for the other machine (Python 3, one file, no packages),
                 from the same commit. Copy it to the Mac or Linux machine and set
                 WASABI_KEY (or ~/.config/wasabi/config: key = ...) to the key Install
                 showed (ENVARC:wasabi.key).
  wasabi_mcp.py  the MCP server for Claude Code and other MCP clients, beside the
                 client (it runs it): claude mcp add wasabi -- python3 wasabi_mcp.py
  wasabi_client.py  the Python API (API 1.0) for your own scripts and test rigs, beside the
                 client: import wasabi_client; with wasabi_client.connect() as amiga: ...

wasabid runs any command the client sends, as you. It answers only clients
with the key, and only from private addresses (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16
and the like); keep the key to yourself. The link is encrypted only when the
Amiga has AmiSSL 5 and keys (wasabi's README). Uninstall removes it.
